raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Kimi-Linear (Kimi Delta Attention + MLA; Kimi K3 uses the same KDA kernels) is not deterministic with `--enable-deterministic-inference`: on MI350X, 2-7 different outputs for 50 identical requests, up to 9 per prompt in the prefix test, and bitwise-identical logprobs in only 10 of 1,275 responses. KDA gives a request different results depending on its batch in three places:
- `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` switches to a row-streaming kernel from 8 requests up, which rounds differently from the Triton kernel;
- `chunk_kda_fwd` fuses the diagonal blocks and the recompute when the batch's total chunk grid is small (`B * NT * H <= 256`): a 59-token sequence alone takes the fused path and inside a batch the unfused one, and the two round differently;
- chunked prefill can split a request off the 64-token chunk grid that `chunk_kda` counts from the sequence start.

## Modifications

- `fla/fused_recurrent.py`: in batch-invariant mode, keep the Triton packed-decode kernel for every batch size.
- `fla/kda.py`: in batch-invariant mode, `chunk_kda_fwd` takes the unfused path for every batch.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: with `--enable-deterministic-inference`, align chunked-prefill splits to 64 tokens for Kimi-Linear models (as already done for Gated DeltaNet models).
- New test `test/registered/amd/test_kda_batch_invariant.py`: a sequence's `chunk_kda` prefill (59, 200 and 1,000 tokens) and a request's packed decode step give the same bits alone and in batches of up to 32.
- Normal mode is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.4, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`, deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference`) together with the other open MI350X deterministic-mode changes (the same in every run). Checks: `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic` (`single`, `prefix`, `prefix --return-logprob`, `radix_cache`, 50 trials) plus a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response). GSM8K through sgl-eval, 1,319 questions, temperature 0.

- Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B TP1: every check passes on 3 / 3 fresh servers (single 1, prefix 1/1/1/1, prefix logprobs identical, radix cache consistent, bitwise 1,275 / 1,275; long-prompt bitwise 9 / 9). Before: single 2-7, prefix up to 9, bitwise 10 / 1,275. GSM8K 91.89% (normal mode 91.28%).
- TP2: every check passes; GSM8K 91.81%.
- The new test passes on MI350X (4 passed). With batch-invariant mode off, 3 of its cases fail (59- and 200-token prefill, packed decode), as expected; the 1,000-token prefill is above the small-grid bound either way.
- Known: at TP4, Kimi-Linear's prefix test still varies (1/2/3/6) with this PR; the same TP4-only symptom appears on another model and is outside KDA.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kimi-Linear TP1, deterministic mode, output throughput 1k / 1k and 8k / 1k: 6,532 / 1,539 -> 6,499 / 1,526 tok/s (-0.5% / -0.8%; normal mode 7,885 / 2,767). Normal mode is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,129 @@
+"""Kimi Delta Attention in batch-invariant mode: a sequence's prefill (chunk_kda) and a
+request's decode step (fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode) must give the same bits alone
+and inside larger batches, although both pick their kernels by batch size otherwise."""
+
+import random
+import sys
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla import fused_recurrent as fused_recurrent_mod
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla import kda as kda_mod
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.fused_recurrent import (
+    fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.kda import chunk_kda
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+
+H, K, V = 32, 128, 128  # Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B at TP1
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _batch_invariant_mode():
+    with (
+        patch.object(kda_mod, "is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled", return_value=True),
+        patch.object(
+            fused_recurrent_mod, "is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled", return_value=True
+        ),
+    ):
+        yield
+
+
+def _randn(*shape, g, scale=1.0):
+    return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device="cuda") * scale).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _sequence(T, g):
+    return [
+        _randn(1, T, H, K, g=g),  # q
+        _randn(1, T, H, K, g=g),  # k
+        _randn(1, T, H, V, g=g),  # v
+        _randn(1, T, H, K, g=g, scale=0.5),  # raw gate
+        torch.rand(1, T, H, generator=g, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16),  # beta
+    ]
+
+
+def _prefill(seqs, A_log, dt_bias):
+    q, k, v, a, beta = (torch.cat([s[i] for s in seqs], dim=1) for i in range(5))
+    lens = [s[0].shape[1] for s in seqs]
+    cu = torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(lens).cumsum(0).tolist()], device="cuda")
+    state = torch.zeros(len(seqs) + 1, H, V, K, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    idx = torch.arange(1, len(seqs) + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    o = chunk_kda(
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        g=a,
+        beta=beta,
+        initial_state=state,
+        initial_state_indices=idx,
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+        cu_seqlens=cu.to(torch.int32),
+        A_log=A_log,
+        dt_bias=dt_bias,
+    )
+    return (o[0] if isinstance(o, tuple) else o), state, cu
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("target_len", [59, 200, 1000])
+def test_chunk_kda_prefill_batch_invariant(target_len):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    A_log = torch.randn(H, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    dt_bias = torch.randn(H * K, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    target = _sequence(target_len, g)
+    alone, alone_state, _ = _prefill([target], A_log, dt_bias)
+    rng = random.Random(target_len)
+    for n in (2, 4, 8, 16, 32):
+        pos = rng.randrange(n)
+        seqs = [_sequence(rng.randint(16, 400), g) for _ in range(n - 1)]
+        seqs.insert(pos, target)
+        out, state, cu = _prefill(seqs, A_log, dt_bias)
+        start = int(cu[pos])
+        assert torch.equal(out[:, start : start + target_len], alone), (
+            f"output, {n} seqs"
+        )
+        assert torch.equal(state[pos + 1], alone_state[1]), f"final state, {n} seqs"
+
+
+def test_kda_packed_decode_batch_invariant():
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1)
+    B = 32
+    mixed_qkv = _randn(B, 2 * H * K + H * V, g=g)
+    a = _randn(B, H * K, g=g, scale=0.5)
+    b = _randn(B, H, g=g)
+    A_log = torch.randn(H, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    dt_bias = torch.randn(H * K, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    state = torch.randn(B, H, V, K, generator=g, device="cuda") * 0.1
+
+    def run(n):
+        s = state[:n].clone()
+        out = mixed_qkv.new_empty(n, 1, H, V)
+        fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode(
+            mixed_qkv=mixed_qkv[:n].contiguous(),
+            a=a[:n].contiguous(),
+            b=b[:n].contiguous(),
+            A_log=A_log,
+            dt_bias=dt_bias,
+            scale=K**-0.5,
+            initial_state=s,
+            out=out,
+            ssm_state_indices=torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+        )
+        return out, s
+
+    ref_out, ref_state = run(1)
+    for n in (2, 4, 7, 8, 16, 32):
+        out, s = run(n)
+        assert torch.equal(out[:1], ref_out), f"output, batch of {n}"
+        assert torch.equal(s[:1], ref_state), f"state, batch of {n}"
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
